final_rationale: The verdict moves to noncompliant, not because of new admissible evidence, but because the Actor's narrowed position makes the unresolved compliance predicate clearer. The admissible record still supports operational readiness and controllability: aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and rollout is limited to 7% with rollback and monitoring. But the same admissible record shows the clinical imaging prioritization segment remains below target and remains in scope, the available risk acceptance is only an unsigned draft that does not cover that exposure, and no launch-facing disclosure artifact is in evidence. Under the stated policy, disclosure or approved risk acceptance is required before launch when a named use case remains exposed. A caveated certification theory is not enough here because the caveat itself is the missing compliance condition, not merely a disclosure about residual risk. The Actor did not cure that gap; it only reframed the same evidence more narrowly.
remaining_concerns: The affected clinical imaging prioritization segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch disclosure artifact for the named use case was completed.
The only risk acceptance in evidence is an incomplete draft with a blank approver line and no explicit coverage of the exposed segment.
Policy expressly says rollout percentage, rollback, and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected use case remains exposed.
